x: Jack Bidgood showed that walking to Brighton gets one fit, by taking third place; and we were glad to see Cornish, on his first appearance with us, making such a good show.

Elson, Heather, Goold, Jarvis, Boddington, Snell Hamer, Spooner, Cornish, Joe Coleman, Earle, Urry, Clark, Pattenden, Willis, True and several others, some beginners, who are showing rapid improvement.

A "B" team, consisting of Boddington, Clark, Cornish, Martin, Snell, Reeve and Sutton also started. From the start our walkers were prominent, together with those of Surrey W.C. and Leicester W.C.—the three teams securing the placings in last year's race.
880 Yards : 1 Morris (M.P.), 2 Cornish (S.), 3 Orton (Bel.). 2 min. 4.3 secs. 1 Mile : 1 Howell (Bel), 2 Edwards (S.), 3 Pettet (M.P.). 4 min. 37.8 secs.
Cornish with Frank Kemp second and Alan Law third. The 880 yards (under 19) saw only four starters and Maurice Jones put in a good finish to beat Maclean, much to the latter's surprise.
Cornish second and Frank Kemp third. The latter ran well off a back mark but is considering taking it easy for the next season or two.
Basil Walden just beat Ron Holtum, with Pete Cornish in third place.
But Sale Harriers weren’t finished yet and as the two London teams slugged it out, Cornish came up three places for the Manchester club and we remained in 5th.
